hints.title: Translate the sum condition
hints.body: For an arithmetic sequence, Sr=r[2a+(r−1)d]2. Property P asks whether Sm=S2m for at least one positive integer m.
hints.recap: The index must remain a positive integer.
hints.pitfall: Opposite signs of a and d alone do not settle an integer existence condition.
hints.pause: Substitute m and 2m in the sum formula and simplify the equality.

recall.reminder: Use the exact endpoints and number of terms when subtracting arithmetic blocks.

hints.body: Cancelling the positive factor <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></math> leads to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>+</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>m</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow></math>. Solve for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi></mrow></math> and test choices of opposite-sign nonzero integers <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></math>.
hints.recap: Existence requires a positive integer index, not just a real solution.
hints.pitfall: Do not drop the integrality condition after rearranging.

hints.title: Test the proposed parity requirement
hints.body: Examine the sum equality with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></math>. Determine what relation it places on the first term and common difference.
hints.recap: Testing necessity requires a successful sequence with the proposed property checked separately.
hints.pitfall: An example where the sum equality fails cannot settle necessity.
hints.pause: Choose nonzero integer values meeting that relation and examine whether an odd difference can work.

solution:
The AP formula gives Sm=m[2a+(m−1)d]2 and S2m=m[2a+(2m−1)d]. Since m>0, equality is equivalent to

2a+(m−1)d=2[2a+(2m−1)d], hence 2a+(3m−1)d=0.

I is false. Choose a=1,d=−3. Then ad=−3<0, but the equation gives 2−3(3m−1)=0, so m=59. There is no positive integer m, and P fails.

II is false. Choose a=1,d=−1,m=1. The sequence begins 1,0,−1,…, so S1=S2=1 even though d is odd. These a and d satisfy the nonzero-integer assumptions.

Answer A: neither statement.
